items.title: Iran war, crude, rupee among 8 factors to steer D-Street in holiday-shortened week
items.description: The Indian stock market faces a holiday-shortened week with significant headwinds. Geopolitical tensions from the Iran-Israel conflict, elevated crude oil prices, and a depreciating rupee are expected to weigh on investor sentiment. Foreign institutional investors continue their selling spree, adding to market uncertainties.

items.title: Stock market open for only 3 days this week. Anand James on how to trade Nifty
items.description: Indian stock markets will trade for only three days this week. This shortened trading period, combined with settlement holidays, is expected to increase market volatility. Investors should be aware of potential deferred reactions to global events. Nifty IT shows resilience, while PSU banks are in a corrective phase.

items.title: Macro shock, macro strength: 9 stocks from different sectors but with one common factor, and upside potential of up to 32%
items.description: When any conflict in the Gulf region escalates, the market usually reacts first and asks questions later. At this juncture, when every stock has suffered another round of decline, investors are probably thinking about what will happen to their portfolios in light of the ongoing war. That instinct is both natural and understandable. But remember: This war will end and the market will get back to doing what it normally does – reward companies with growth and earnings.

items.title: Market trading guide: Buy ACME Solar and Dalmia Bharat on Monday for short-term gains up to 16%. Here’s why
items.description: Nifty snapped its two-day rally amid weak sentiment driven by Iran-US tensions, high energy prices, and a falling rupee. Technical indicators signal continued bearish momentum. Experts suggest a sell-on-rise strategy, while recommending ACME Solar and Dalmia Bharat as bullish breakout trades with near-term upside potential.

items.title: 13 penny stocks plunge up to 90% in FY26. Are you affected?
items.description: In fiscal year 2026 (FY26), 13 penny stocks recorded sharp declines, falling between 50% and 90%. These underperformers were identified through a targeted screening approach focused on stocks with a market capitalisation below Rs 1,000 crore, a share price under Rs 20, and a minimum recent trading volume of 50 lakh shares. The strategy aims to highlight low-priced, actively traded penny stocks that have experienced significant downside. (Data Source: ACE Equity)Although penny stocks often attract investors with their low entry prices and potential for rapid gains, they come with substantial risks. Due to low liquidity, high volatility, and limited transparency, they are prone to manipulation and sudden price drops. Without a clear strategy and strong risk controls, investors may face more losses than gains.

items.title: War is profitable, time to get richer: 'Rich Dad Poor Dad' author Robert Kiyosaki
items.description: Amid rising Iran-US-Israel tensions and surging oil prices, Robert Kiyosaki warned that wars, while tragic, are financially profitable for some. He highlighted inflation risks, rising debt, and wealth erosion, urging financial education and disciplined investing. Kiyosaki also reiterated that market crashes could create opportunities for prepared investors.

items.title: Dividend, bonus issue alert: IREDA among 12 stocks turning ex-date for corporate actions this week. Do you own any?
items.description: Around 12 stocks will turn ex-date for corporate actions such as dividends, bonus issues, rights issues and stock splits in the holiday-shortened week between March 30 (Monday) and April 3 (Friday). Stocks likely to be in focus include Gujarat Cotex, IRB Infrastructure Developers, Triton Valves, TVS Motor Company, Aster DM Healthcare, B2B Software Technologies, Chennai Petroleum Corporation, CRISIL, Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA), R&B Denims, TVS Holdings and Sundaram-Clayton.

items.title: 8 midcap stocks with massive upside potential of up to 75%. Do you own any?
items.description: Analyst forecasts are more than just numbers; they provide a forward-looking perspective on market potential. For investors on the lookout for the next breakout opportunities, a fresh analysis of BSE mid-cap stocks highlights several compelling prospects.Based on consensus estimates from market analysts, Trendlyne data suggests that several mid-cap stocks could deliver strong returns over the next 12 months. This projected upside represents the average expected gain during this period, providing a data-driven roadmap for investors seeking high-potential mid-cap opportunities. We highlight eight standout mid-cap stocks with estimated upside potential ranging from 40% to 65% over the coming year.
